pi_results.name: Chi-square goodness of fit
pi_results.expected_description: mean of the chi-square distribution (its degrees of freedom)
pi_results.interpretation: If the digits behaved like independent digits, each equally likely to be 0-9, a result at least this extreme would be expected in about 41% of samples. The data are compatible with the model on this measure.
assumptions: Expected count per cell is at least 5.
limitations: Describes only the finite range analysed. It says nothing about digits outside it and cannot prove or disprove that pi is normal.
A large p-value is an absence of evidence against the model, not evidence that the digits are random.

pi_results.name: Shannon entropy
pi_results.expected_description: log2(10) minus the small-sample bias expected for uniform digits; the maximum possible value is 3.321928
pi_results.interpretation: The digit distribution carries 3.321254 bits per digit, 99.9797% of the maximum for ten symbols. Entropy close to the maximum means single digits are close to equally frequent.
assumptions: Entropy is computed from single-digit frequencies only.
limitations: First-order entropy ignores order: 0123456789 repeated forever also reaches the maximum.
The plug-in estimate is biased slightly downward in finite samples.
Describes only the finite range analysed. It says nothing about digits outside it and cannot prove or disprove that pi is normal.

pi_results.name: Autocorrelation (Ljung-Box)
pi_results.expected_description: mean of the chi-square distribution (number of lags)
pi_results.null_hypothesis: digit values are uncorrelated at lags 1 to 3
pi_results.interpretation: If the digits behaved like independent digits, each equally likely to be 0-9, a result at least this extreme would be expected in about 64% of samples. The data are compatible with the model on this measure. The largest single autocorrelation is -0.01110 at lag 1; for this sample size values within about 0.01960 of zero are ordinary.
assumptions: Under the null model each autocorrelation is approximately normal with standard deviation 1/sqrt(n).
Digits are treated as numbers 0-9, so only linear dependence is measured.
limitations: Only linear dependence between digit values at the tested lags is detected.
Describes only the finite range analysed. It says nothing about digits outside it and cannot prove or disprove that pi is normal.
A large p-value is an absence of evidence against the model, not evidence that the digits are random.

pi_results.name: Runs test (Wald-Wolfowitz)
pi_results.expected_description: z-score expected when the order of symbols is random
pi_results.null_hypothesis: the order of digits 5-9 and digits 0-4 is random
pi_results.interpretation: If the digits behaved like independent digits, each equally likely to be 0-9, a result at least this extreme would be expected in about 70% of samples. The data are compatible with the model on this measure. There are 5,020 runs, more than the 5,001.0 expected.
assumptions: Digits are recoded into two symbols: digits 5-9 versus digits 0-4.
The number of runs is approximately normal, which needs a large sample.
limitations: Recoding to two symbols discards most of the information in the digits.
Describes only the finite range analysed. It says nothing about digits outside it and cannot prove or disprove that pi is normal.
A large p-value is an absence of evidence against the model, not evidence that the digits are random.

pi_results.name: N-gram distribution (2-digit blocks)
pi_results.expected_description: mean of the chi-square distribution (its degrees of freedom)
pi_results.null_hypothesis: all 100 possible 2-digit blocks are equally likely
pi_results.interpretation: If the digits behaved like independent digits, each equally likely to be 0-9, a result at least this extreme would be expected in about 19% of samples. The data are compatible with the model on this measure.
assumptions: The sequence is cut into 5,000 non-overlapping blocks of 2 digits, which are independent under the null model.
Expected count per block value is at least 5.
limitations: Describes only the finite range analysed. It says nothing about digits outside it and cannot prove or disprove that pi is normal.
A large p-value is an absence of evidence against the model, not evidence that the digits are random.

note: Simulated sequences come from a pseudo-random generator and show the spread each statistic has by chance. Pi's digits are fixed, not random; agreement with the simulations means pi is statistically indistinguishable from them on these measures in this range, not that pi is random. The percentile is descriptive, not a p-value.
